observed: The released #[tool] get_session_id handler accepts RequestContext<RoleServer> and reads ctx.extensions.get::<axum::http::request::Parts>().

The same released file demonstrates typed tool argument extraction with Parameters<StructRequest> in sum(), and RequestContext plus Parameters together are supported in handler-style signatures elsewhere in the file.

The released get_session_id example treats missing HTTP Parts as a normal no-session result; that permissive behavior is suitable for diagnostics only and must not be copied for an authenticated task-materialization path.

slice.finding: For an authenticated persistent-task tool, the minimal application-owned guard belongs at the beginning of the registered tool handler, after rmcp has delivered RequestContext/typed arguments but before any task-store lookup that can create or mutate an operation. Read http::request::Parts from RequestContext.extensions, then read Principal from parts.extensions. If either Parts or Principal is absent, return an authentication/authorization error immediately and perform zero persistent create-or-get work. With Principal present, evaluate current policy against the authenticated principal, tool identity and validated arguments; denial also returns before create-or-get. Only after those checks may a stable operation identity be bound and an atomic persistent create-or-get be attempted. Client `_meta` is not identity authority.
fail_closed_contract: Missing RequestContext HTTP Parts => reject before task-store access.
Missing server-authenticated Principal in parts.extensions => reject before task-store access.
Current-policy denial or revocation => reject before task create-or-get even when a continuation token is otherwise valid.
Policy input is authenticated Principal plus current tool/validated arguments; client metadata cannot substitute for Principal.
The first persistent task mutation is strictly after principal extraction and current-policy authorization.
source_scope_limits: The exact released rmcp example proves RequestContext-to-HTTP-Parts extraction, not an rmcp-provided Principal type or authentication policy engine.
Principal insertion/extraction and the fail-closed auth error are application-owned composition; this slice did not compile a concrete Principal type or select a specific McpError constructor.
This slice does not inspect persistent task execution, restart redrive, external-effect idempotency/fencing, credential verification, revocation transport, or confidentiality.
